summaries.demographer: Michael Jones is a 19-year-old White, non-Hispanic male living with his parents and younger sister in Sundance, Wyoming (Q51, Q84-Q89). He has completed 11th grade but has no diploma, is not enrolled in school, and is not currently in the paid workforce (Q90-Q92, Q69-Q73). His household appears stable but modest, with parents covering mortgage and expenses while he remains financially dependent (Q55-Q58, Q83). His life course is marked by delayed educational completion, family co-residence, and a transition from adolescent schooling into an uncertain creative-career pathway (Q01-Q04, Q108).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Michael shows present-bias and avoidance under anxiety: he misses deadlines, delays bills or forms, and over-edits portfolio work instead of submitting it (Q44, Q83). At the same time, he responds well to external accountability, named savings goals, and structured commitments like library volunteering (Q17, Q61, Q78). His consumption preferences reveal identity-based spending on art supplies and software, sometimes at odds with limited income (Q56, Q83). He is risk-aware about debt and prefers scholarships, community college, and incremental certifications over expensive schooling (Q62-Q63, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Michael is registered unaffiliated and identifies as an Independent who currently leans closer to the Democratic Party on education, health care, environment, libraries, and social issues (Q23-Q24, Q95-Q96). His political outlook blends rural Wyoming localism and self-reliance with growing support for public services and social inclusion (Q24-Q25). He has moderate civic attachment through church, library volunteering, local events, and concern for local elections, but he is not yet a consistent voter (Q23, Q47, Q65). On race and policing, he reports learning and discussion rather than activism, reflecting awareness shaped by online networks more than local diversity (Q26-Q30).
summaries.psychologist: Michael presents as imaginative, conscientious in aspiration, socially responsive, and prone to anxiety-driven avoidance and perfectionism (Q01, Q44-Q45). His self-concept centers on creative potential, usefulness, and independence, but he struggles when adult milestones require bureaucratic follow-through (Q34, Q83, Q109). He regulates emotion through hiking, meditation, journaling, art-making, humor, and trusted relationships with his mother and close friends (Q31, Q43, Q49-Q50). He shows strong identity integration between rural belonging and digital artistic culture, which gives him both grounding and tension about where he fits (Q08, Q47-Q48, Q108).
